note: GENESIS-PILOT FIXTURE (14-concept batch, drafted 2026-08-22).
Fixtures-first for the new `envy-and-jealousy` concept; PENDING until
the pack lands, then flip active in the same PR.
Proverbs 27:4 is asserted: IN the fixture corpus, carries 'jealousy'
lexically, and this pack is its only anchoring concept, so the reason
chip is unambiguous. The narrative exemplars (Gen 4, Gen 37, 1 Sam 18)
and the teaching verse Prov 14:30 are all OUT of the fixture corpus —
see the pack's corpus-needs note.
The preferredOrder pair follows the sense-inversion-provision ruling
(Jesse, 2026-08-15): Exodus 20:5 — 'I, the LORD your God, am a jealous
God' — is an honest lexical match for the query word in its OPPOSITE
register: a searcher struggling with envy served divine covenant
jealousy. It is demoted, never forbidden; both references are in the
fixture corpus, so the pair cannot pass vacuously.
CORPUS-EXPANSION EXECUTION (ruling rows 24-25, approved 2026-08-26):
the narrative exemplars this pack's corpus-needs note named (Gen 4,
Gen 37, 1 Sam 18) and Prov 14:30 are now in corpus. The bare-word
queries kept here still hold Prov 27:4 in the top 3 unchanged
(measured #1 for 'jealousy', #3 for 'envy'); the two phrase queries,
where the exemplars lead, move to their own fixture
(envy-and-jealousy-phrases.json) with the ruling's widened window,
because per-query windows are not in the schema and the bare-word
top-3 assertion must not be weakened by the split.
SUPPLEMENT ROW S1 (approved as proposed, 2026-08-30): on the full
release bed Jas 3:14-16's regenerated preached vocabulary ('envy')
honestly outranks Prov 27:4 for the bare word, measuring it at #4
(bare 'jealousy' still holds the top 3). Row-29's approved
principle, window-widening only: Prov 27:4 -> top 5 for this
bare-word fixture. The Ex 20:5 sense-inversion preferredOrder is
untouched. Folded into this PR because the catch-up PR the
supplement named as S1's venue does not exist; the supplement
itself offered the one-vehicle fold.
